dayConvention: Day numbering: the first day with impressions is day 1, and the first N days are days 1 to N. Stage bands: 1-3, 4-7, 8-14, 15-30, 31+. A learning reset restarts the count at day 1 on the reset date. All in the account timezone.
note: Moshi's Sales campaign was created paused on Sep 25 and first delivered 2026-09-27: day 17 today, next gate day 31 on 2026-10-27. Its new ad set, Moshi | Chat | Gift guide (1202700000000022), was created paused on Oct 9 (startTime 2026-10-09T16:30:00-0700) and first delivered Oct 10, so it launched Oct 10 (day 4 today), and the first ad set delivered every day before it. The report window is the 7 days before Oct 10: 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-09, with window.before 1202700000000022 and partial false. get_ad_performance's window (2026-09-27 to 2026-10-13, since_launch) is moshiWindow: every Moshi count and the chatters cover it, and the report prints those dates next to them. The primary campaign is the Moshi Sales campaign, the only Moshi campaign.
window: Traps: the gift guide's startTime is Oct 9, so a run that takes startTime as the launch sets Oct 2 to Oct 8, which check 16 flags. A run that keeps get_ad_performance's window mixes the gift guide's learning days into every Meta number. Stages and gates count to today: day 15 fell on Oct 11, after the window ended, so the next gate is day 31 on 2026-10-27, not day 15. The gift guide's launch is in changes[] (new_ad, source moshi); its first cost-per-chat read is day 4, today, and its first CPA read day 8, 2026-10-17.
running: T7 (2026-10-03 to 2026-10-09, owner merchant, maxAds 500) lists all 17 merchant ads. Each merchant ad set's totals are T7's ad set metrics, with linkClicks summed from its ads' funnel.linkClicks. The running entry compares the primary's CTR over the window (2.23%) with Evergreen | ASC | US, RTG | Site + IG 30d and Fall Tins | Launch, each campaign's CTR weighted by its spend: 1.41% ($6,484 of spend). Pooling every click gives 1.41% here too; negative/running.data.js is the test that separates them. Brand | Video views optimizes for ThruPlay, so it maps to other and stays out. RTG | Site + IG 30d is mostly broad (its Broad 25-54 ad set holds about 80% of its spend): it counts, and no text may call it retargeting. The gold flags only its Site visitors 30d ad set as retargeting; marking the whole campaign passes too, since the flag only keeps a launch out of a launch comparison and RTG is not a launch.
launch: Fall Tins | Launch (whole campaign, started Sep 15) is the only launch: CTR over days 1-13 (day 13 is Moshi's age on the window's last day, Oct 9), by merchantCampaignId. A cpc comparison on the same pair also passes. No CPA or ROAS comparison: the Moshi ad set had 4 purchases in the last 7 days, under the ~50 floor. Evergreen and RTG are mature; Brand | Video views is other.
chatters: list_conversations (limit 100, sinceDays reaching Sep 27) returns 100 of 144 rows with page.hasNext true, so the run calls it again with the same arguments and cursor set to page.nextCursor, which returns the other 44 (hasNext false). Everyone is listed, so chatters.total is null and the report shows no partial-coverage line: that line is only the fallback when a page fails. The 144 rows: 141 on Instagram and 3 on Messenger, the 6 who used the profile's message button among them (chats 144, chatsFromAds 138). Buyers (purchaseCount above 0): ana.brews (verified, 48.2k followers, $86), kettle.kate (3.4k, $58), slowpour.sam (1,180, two orders: $31 + $43.50 = $74.50), moss.and.mint ($44), dee.reads ($39), early.oolong ($52, only on the second page) and Priya Natarajan on Messenger ($61), each orderValue from its purchase_complete events: 8 orders, $414.50, as get_ad_performance says. The rest take their stage from get_leads (flow_entry reads as messaged). threadUrl comes straight from each row: Business Suite links for Instagram, Page-inbox links on facebook.com for Messenger, and null where Meta did not return the thread (dee.reads, steeped.daily, Grace Whitfield and a few others), so those rows get no paper-plane. Trap: oolong.otto's lastMessage holds an email address, which must not appear in DATA or the reply.

dataSource: Tree reads T1-T5 and T7 are moshi-mcp's own shapeAdTree (origin/main) over a mocked GET /meta-api/ad-tree, as in the other fixtures. Moshi's ads carry clonedFrom null and no creativeOverlap (the tool leaves an empty one out), so there is no T6, no Same ads and no overlap callout. T1, T3 and T4 carry the expected ads_over_max_ads flag, which stays out of flags[]. The Moshi tools' outputs follow the other fixtures' modelled shapes, with the MCP's real window shape (since, displayUntil, period); list_conversations, get_leads, get_conversation_events, get_closer_activity and get_conversation_messages follow moshi-api's DTOs. partial_period comes from the Moshi tools, whose window ends today.
